raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies assembled, rearrangeable organizers with no recorded damage claims (D2-O7), but observed time, component reports and unaided arrangement fall short of the intended outcomes (D2-O2–O4). Assembly, selection, checking and instruction problems remain plausible contributors; their shares are unmeasured. Repeated three-compartment orders taking seven to nine minutes while mixed batches contain every extreme delay supports investigating order variation, but does not separate switching from layout complexity (D2-O6). A concrete limiting observation is overlapping widths among first-attempt and retry partitions (D2-O5): width alone cannot cleanly classify insertion difficulty. No mechanism is established.

openings.claim: Order switching and shared-bin selection may contribute to delays and component errors; temporary order-specific staging with a component-count check may reduce both.
openings.delta: Test selection and checking separately from insertion, while retaining full assembly and every accepted configuration.
openings.prediction: For comparable layouts and workers, staged orders have shorter selection/checking times and fewer independently detected component discrepancies; unchanged insertion time would distinguish this account from an insertion bottleneck.
openings.probe: Use up to 15 sample organizers in matched, counterbalanced current-versus-staged cycles across layouts and both workers. Record each work stage, staging overhead, color and component correctness. Reuse samples; inspect for wear. Cost staging before adoption and measure total assembly/packing time, including staging.
assumptions: Temporary staging fits the existing bench and stated budgets.
Testing and any rollout fit the fixed delivery date.
Repeated sample handling does not materially distort timings.

openings.claim: Does a diagram showing the ordered layout resolve short-partition confusion when contents are independently verified complete?
openings.delta: Discriminate instruction ambiguity from difficulties persisting with correct parts and layout-specific guidance.
openings.prediction: Instruction ambiguity predicts fewer placement questions with the ordered-layout diagram; persistent confusion would weaken that account.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten participants, balanced by layout, to current or ordered-layout diagrams using verified-complete samples. Record unaided success, time and exact failure step. Treat five per condition as exploratory, then verify pilot outcomes separately.
assumptions: Diagram substitution fits cost and delivery limits.
Samples preserve footprint, assortment, removable partitions, selected counts and color.

raw.assessment: Two proposed reuses of supplied resources merit bounded tests. Neither is established to achieve the pilot targets. Mixed-batch delays do not identify their cause, and overlapping widths do not identify the insertion problem.

openings.claim: Reuse the geometry recorded by existing cutting templates to make reusable board silhouettes for checking each order's complete partition set before insertion and packing.
openings.delta: Manufacturing geometry becomes a contents-checking surface: one position per required partition, including repeated shapes, could expose omissions and substitutions.
openings.prediction: A matched trial will detect more deliberately omitted or substituted partitions than the current check; separately timed checking and selection will reveal whether this reduces total work.
openings.probe: First verify template revisions against actual parts and independently confirmed component lists for accepted layouts. Use spare board for sample checking surfaces. Compare seeded-error detection and separately timed workflow stages across both workers and mixed layouts. Check exterior color against the order slip separately.
assumptions: Templates are explicitly available, but sufficient shape distinction and correct revision are unverified.
Fixture preparation must fit the fixed delivery date and 500-unit budget; added per-order material cost must remain at most 0.40.
This does not establish customer arrangement success.

openings.claim: Reuse the existing three-layout diagram as an order-specific placement reference by identifying the selected layout and explicitly pointing out the short partition's location.
openings.delta: An existing packing insert carries the customer's chosen arrangement and a targeted placement cue.
openings.prediction: With complete, correct parts, first-attempt short-partition placement will improve and requests for location help will decrease.
openings.probe: Verify that the incumbent diagram actually represents each accepted arrangement and current parts. Randomly assign the ten participants to existing versus revised diagrams; record unaided completion and short-partition placement before offering help. Treat results as preliminary; measure annotation time and cost.
assumptions: The diagram's existence is supplied; its coverage and economical editing method are unverified.
Product geometry, assortment, compartment counts, color and dismantling remain intact; preparation must respect budget and delivery constraints.

openings.claim: Order staging/count checks may reduce switching/selection delays and errors.
openings.discriminator: Selection/checking improves while insertion stays unchanged.
openings.probe: Counterbalance current/staged cycles across workers/layouts with <=15 reusable samples; time all stages/overhead, verify counts/color, inspect wear.
openings.uncertainty: Layout complexity confounds switching; bench fit and reuse effects unknown.

openings.claim: Template silhouettes, including duplicate positions, may expose omissions/substitutions.
openings.discriminator: Improved seeded-error detection versus current checks; total time exposes overhead.
openings.probe: Verify template revisions, parts and independent component lists; test spare-board surfaces across workers/mixed layouts; check color separately.
openings.uncertainty: Shape distinction unverified; customer arrangement untested.

openings.claim: Ordered-layout guidance with a short-partition cue may resolve confusion.
openings.discriminator: Better first placement/fewer questions support instruction ambiguity; persistent confusion weakens it.
openings.probe: Verify diagram coverage/current parts; randomize ten participants, balance layouts, compare current/revised diagrams with verified-complete sets. Record unaided success/time, placement/failure step and annotation overhead.
openings.uncertainty: Five per condition: exploratory; cue/layout effects combined.

post_distill.decision: Probe before adoption; preserve 30x20 cm footprint, assortment, removability, accepted counts/colors and deadline; costs <=500 initially and <=0.40/order. Verify 60-order targets separately: >=98% complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided arrangement. Synthetic observations establish no mechanism; overlapping widths cannot identify insertion difficulty.
